entities.summary: Cineas (b. 399 BCE, Thessaly) was a renowned explorer and navigator of the Classical era, active in Thessaly. He is best known for his voyages along the Mediterranean coast and his discovery of the western route to the Black Sea. Cineas was a key figure in the Thessalian League, a powerful confederation of city-states that played a significant role in shaping the politics of the region. He was a close associate of the Spartan general Brasidas, and his expeditions often coincided with Brasidas' military campaigns. Cineas' voyages also had a profound impact on the development of trade and commerce in the region, as he established trade routes between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean. His legacy extended beyond his own time, as his discoveries and explorations influenced later generations of navigators and traders. Cineas' name is still remembered in the annals of Thessalian history, and his bravery and skill as an explorer are still celebrated by historians today. The exact date of his death remains unknown, but it is believed to have been sometime in the late 4th century BCE.
